# Rebuttal Pre-drafted Responses

## Q1: Limited Environment Generalization

We thank the reviewer for raising the question of environment coverage. Our study is designed as a diagnostic investigation: the primary goal is to establish a causal chain from temporal embedding co-adaptation to value overestimation and policy collapse, not to maximize benchmark breadth. To this end, we demonstrate that the same causal mechanism reproduces across environments with substantially different reward scales (Walker, mean return ~918 vs. Cheetah, ~625) and qualitatively distinct dynamics (a 6-joint biped vs. a 2-joint runner). Notably, the absolute strength of the CIVO effect varies considerably across these environments (Walker NVE ranges from 1.5x to 4x while Cheetah NVE ranges from 8x to 70x), yet the underlying causal sequence remains invariant: trained temporal embeddings combined with multi-rate exposure produce value overestimation that precipitates collapse. We further include PickCube-v1 as a third evaluation environment on a second simulator (ManiSkill, distinct from DeepMind Control Suite) to verify detector specificity, extending coverage beyond locomotion tasks. We acknowledge in the Limitations section that broader architecture and environment generalization remains an open direction for future work.

## Q2: Threshold Circularity / Overfitting

We appreciate the reviewer's concern regarding potential circularity in threshold selection. The NVE threshold of 1.5x was calibrated exclusively on a Walker-only factorial subset of n=10 runs, then validated without recalibration on the full n=16 set that includes Cheetah runs, achieving 15/16 correct classifications. This held-out validation confirms that the threshold transfers across environments without post-hoc adjustment. More importantly, we report AUROC=0.953 as our primary discriminative metric; AUROC is rank-based and entirely independent of any particular threshold choice, providing a threshold-free measure of diagnostic power. Leave-one-out cross-validation on the n=10 Walker calibration subset yields AUROC values in the range [0.944, 1.000], confirming that no single run disproportionately influences the threshold. The sole false positive (run 008e_v3_s2) exhibits a mechanistically distinct, non-CIVO collapse mode, which indicates that the NVE threshold captures the broader phenomenon of value overestimation rather than being narrowly fitted to one failure pattern.

## Q3: Architecture Generalization

We appreciate this important question. Our claim is precisely scoped to "imagination-based actor-critic architectures with learned temporal embeddings," and we deliberately avoid generalizing to all reinforcement learning methods. The TAWM comparison directly isolates the role of feedback architecture: TAWM uses the same RSSM world model but replaces imagination-based bootstrapping with re-planning, and CIVO does not manifest. This result demonstrates that the failure originates in the feedback loop of imagined rollouts rather than in RSSM per se. At the mechanistic level, CIVO requires three structural ingredients: (1) temporal embeddings that co-adapt with the value function through shared gradient flow, (2) multi-step imagined rollouts used for critic training, and (3) a reward head that inherits latent biases from a shared representation. These conditions are defined functionally and are not tied to any specific network topology. We identify transformer-based world models as an explicit future direction in Section 7, and we believe the diagnostic contribution of this paper, identifying and characterizing a previously undocumented failure mode, holds independent value from exhaustive architectural enumeration.
